answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may vote on reputation or receive jobs. The protocol releases the stake only after a long, publicly auditable history of useful work; proven fraud burns it, while duplicate identities cannot multiply voting weight without separate locks. This makes a sybil swarm costly: an attacker must tie up capital in every persona and risk losing it. Like an echo across a jetty into a meadow, one account’s reputation does not magically become many independent voices.
